info.name: WeAreDA Reseller Reference
info.description:
Every request in the WeAreDA reseller integration, in both directions.

    WeAreDA -> Reseller   folders 01-04 and parts of 10
                          calls INTO your commerce/ERP system
                          auth: X-API-Key (or bearer / basic / custom)

    Reseller -> WeAreDA   folders 05-08 and parts of 10
                          the signed webhook you call
                          auth: HMAC-SHA256 over the exact raw body

    Reseller -> WeAreDA   folders 00 and 09
    (management API)      the connect API and the read API on WeAreDA's
                          backend
                          auth: X-Reseller-Key

THREE DIFFERENT CREDENTIALS. They are not interchangeable.

Webhook requests sign themselves: a pre-request script builds the event,
serializes it ONCE, signs those exact bytes and sets X-WeAreDA-Signature,
X-WeAreDA-Event-Id and X-WeAreDA-Timestamp. The request body is the same
string that was signed.

Folder 00 registers the integration. integrationMode decides which of folders
01-04 apply to you at all - a receive_only reseller implements none of them and
still works, publishing through folders 05-08. Inbound webhooks work in every
mode.

Suggested order: 00 -> 01 -> 02 -> 03 (captures orderId) -> 05/07/08 -> 04.

Remember while you test: orders and stock are independent flows. Nothing in
folders 03 or 04 changes stock anywhere, on either side.

item.name: 00 - Integration Configuration
item.description:
Direction: Reseller -> WeAreDA management API (X-Reseller-Key), contract 1.1, 2 and 6.1.

integrationMode and orderStatusWrite are TOP-LEVEL fields of the connect body,
siblings of orderDeliveryStatus. Inside declaredCapabilities they are
400 invalid_request; inside syncConfig, 400 invalid_sync_config.

    integrationMode    reads  order delivery  catalog
    query_and_send     yes    yes             pull      (default)
    receive_and_send   NO     yes             push
    query_only         yes    NO              pull
    receive_only       NO     NO              push

Inbound webhooks (folders 05-08) work in EVERY mode. The mode governs only
what WeAreDA does.

Point wearedaApiBaseUrl at `npm run mock:weareda` (http://localhost:4000) to
run this folder without a real WeAreDA connection.

request.description:
The default shape: WeAreDA reads your catalog on a schedule AND delivers orders to you.

You implement all four calls: GET /, GET /products, POST /orders, POST /orders/{id}/cancel.

The response echoes integrationMode, orderDeliveryEnabled and productsSyncMode, and captures webhookUrl into the collection variable used by folders 05-08.

syncConfig.orders.requiresTaxId (contract 4.3.2, 7) - a boolean, default
false, which is the behaviour every existing integration keeps.

true means WeAreDA NEVER delivers an order whose customer has no fiscal
identifier: the order is simply not yet eligible, and it is delivered
automatically - within a minute - once the tenant completes the contact.
Nothing is parked and nothing has to be re-queued.

That is the setting for a reseller that cannot invoice without a tax id.
Rejecting such orders on arrival is the wrong answer: a non-auth 4xx is not
retried, so it turns a waiting order into a manual-review ticket.

Unlike integrationMode and orderStatusWrite, this one IS a syncConfig option -
it configures a delivery rule, not the shape of the integration. A non-boolean
value is 400 invalid_sync_config.

item.name: connect - receive_and_send (no read endpoint, orders still arrive)

request.description:
Reads OFF, order delivery ON.

WeAreDA never calls GET / or GET /products; your catalog arrives as product.updated webhooks (folder 06). Orders are still DELIVERED - delivering an order is a send, not a query.

No sync schedule is created, and any schedule left by a previous connect is deleted.

item.name: connect - query_only (read from, never sent an order)

request.description:
Reads ON, order delivery OFF.

ordersWrite is switched off in the effective capabilities, so orders never enter the delivery queue at all. Nothing is queued and later refused.

Note the explicit "orderStatusWrite": false. Omitting a field on a reconnect leaves the STORED value unchanged - so if this tenant already had the opt-in on, moving it to a mode that delivers no orders must turn the flag off in the same call, or the connect is refused with 400 invalid_request.

exec: pm.test('ordersWrite is off in the effective capabilities', function () {

item.name: connect - receive_only (publish only, baseUrl still required)

request.description:
Nothing is ever called on your side. You only publish webhooks.

A baseUrl is STILL required at connect time - it is registered, not called. Omitting it is 400 invalid_request.

Note the explicit "orderStatusWrite": false. Omitting a field on a reconnect leaves the STORED value unchanged - so if this tenant already had the opt-in on, moving it to a mode that delivers no orders must turn the flag off in the same call, or the connect is refused with 400 invalid_request.

Opt in to letting an inbound order.status move the CUSTOMER-FACING orders.status, not just integration_status (contract 6.1).

Strict boolean. Per TENANT, unlike integrationMode which is per reseller.

With this on, a status move fires the same alerts and conversation-lifecycle automation a manual change in the CRM fires, and shipped_at / delivered_at are filled in when blank.

Echoes integrationMode, orderDeliveryEnabled, productsSyncMode and orderStatusWrite, plus the validated syncConfig that was stored.

syncSchedule is null in a mode that does not read.

exec: pm.test('echoes the three derived fields', function () {

item.name: POST test-connection (422 read_calls_disabled in a receive_* mode)

request.description:
Asks WeAreDA to call GET / on your baseUrl.

THE CONNECTION TEST IS A READ. Run this after connecting in receive_and_send or receive_only and it answers 422 { reason: 'read_calls_disabled' } without calling anything - there is nothing for it to test.

After a query_* connect it actually calls you: watch the GET / arrive in your sandbox log.

item.name: 400 invalid_request - orderStatusWrite on a mode without order delivery

request.description:
The one combination that is refused:

  orderStatusWrite requires an integrationMode that delivers orders -
  'query_only' never sends this reseller an order to report a status on

The two settings are otherwise independent: integrationMode is per reseller and describes topology; orderStatusWrite is per tenant and is a question of data authority.
orderStatusWrite must be a REAL boolean. The string "true" is a 400, not a truthy value.

WRONG PLACE. integrationMode is a TOP-LEVEL field, a sibling of orderDeliveryStatus.

declaredCapabilities accepts only six boolean keys - productsRead, productsWrite, stockRead, stockWebhooks, ordersWrite, invoices - and it is METADATA ONLY. Effective capabilities are connector support n platform ceiling n mode; your declaration is not an input and enables nothing.

WRONG PLACE, and a different error code than the declaredCapabilities mistake.

Unknown keys INSIDE syncConfig are rejected loudly (contract 7). Unknown keys at the TOP LEVEL of the body are dropped in silence - see the next request.

The mode DERIVES the catalog transport: pull for query_*, push for receive_*.

Setting a contradictory products.mode is a 400, not a precedence rule. To push, choose receive_and_send or receive_only - do not fight the derivation.

item.name: 200 but silently ignored - productsSyncMode at the top level

request.description:
THE SILENT ONE. productsSyncMode is a RESPONSE field, never an input.

Sent at the top level of the connect body it is dropped without a word: 200, no error, and productsSyncMode in the response is still 'pull'. This is the failure that looks exactly like a feature that does not work.

Unknown keys inside syncConfig are the opposite - rejected loudly.

exec: pm.test('the input was dropped without a word', function () {

item.name: 03 - Orders
item.description:
POST /orders - contract 4.3. Idempotent on Idempotency-Key, and ALWAYS returns the reseller order id.

Receiving an order changes NO stock (contract 6.4).

request.description:
Direction: WeAreDA -> Reseller.

The delivered order. Note it carries NO external_order_id: WeAreDA identifies it by order_number + idempotency_key, and adopts YOUR id from the response.

Saves the returned id into the `orderId` variable.

The `customer` object (contract 4.3, added 2026-09) is OPTIONAL and ADDITIVE:
  - the whole key is OMITTED when the order has no contact;
  - customer.tax_id is NULL when the contact has no fiscal identification - the
    key is always present INSIDE customer, so you can branch on it directly;
  - tax_id.type is a FREE SHORT TOKEN, not an enum (CUIT, CUIL, DNI, CPF, CNPJ,
    NIF, NIE, CIF, RFC, EIN, SSN, VAT, TAX_ID, ...). An unknown value is normal:
    accept it verbatim, never normalise it, NEVER reject the order over it;
  - tax_id.country is ISO 3166-1 alpha-2;
  - the values are a SNAPSHOT taken when the order was created (4.3.1). Do not
    expect them to match a later read of the customer, and never 'correct' a
    stored order from one. An order that arrived with no fiscal id may report
    one later - the snapshot freezes a value, not an absence.

If you cannot invoice without a fiscal id, set syncConfig.orders.requiresTaxId:
true (4.3.2, folder 00) - WeAreDA then never delivers such an order, and
delivers it automatically within a minute of the tenant completing the contact.
Rejecting the delivery is the wrong answer: a non-auth 4xx is not retried.

The identifier below is deliberately fake. The sandbox MASKS it in every log
line and in GET /debug/orders (20-******78-9) and keeps the real value only on
the order it invoices against (11.8).

request.description:
Direction: WeAreDA -> Reseller.

KENNITALA is Iceland's national identifier. Nothing in this repository has
heard of it, and the order is accepted anyway, with the token stored exactly
as it arrived.

tax_id.type is a FREE SHORT TOKEN, not an enum (contract 4.3). Meeting a
value you do not recognise is NORMAL. Never reject it, never normalise it
into a type you do know, and never add a list of 'valid' types - the next
country will not be on it.

Check GET /debug/orders afterwards: the order is there, with its tax id
masked in the view and stored in full underneath.

request.description:
Direction: WeAreDA -> Reseller.

The contact has no fiscal identification, so tax_id is NULL. The key is
always present inside customer, so branching on it needs no guessing
(contract 4.3).

This is an ordinary order and must be accepted. A 4xx here is not retried:
it would route the order to manual_review for a human to rescue.

If your billing cannot issue an invoice without a fiscal id, the answer is
syncConfig.orders.requiresTaxId: true (contract 4.3.2, folder 00) - WeAreDA
then holds the order back and delivers it automatically, within a minute, as
soon as the tenant completes the contact. Nothing is parked or re-queued.

Run `npm run cli -- invoice <id>` on the created order to see what the
invoice flow prints when there is no fiscal identity.

written before it keeps working untouched. Never make customer required.

item.name: 05 - WeAreDA Webhooks
item.description: The signed inbound webhook - contract 6.1. One event type per HTTP request, always.

exec: // The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over the EXACT RAW BODY BYTES that are sent.
// So we build the event, serialize it ONCE into `signedBody`, sign THAT
// string, and let the request body be exactly {{signedBody}}.
// Never re-stringify after signing - different bytes mean 401 unauthorized.
console.warn('webhookSecret is not set - WeAreDA will answer 401 unauthorized.');
const event = { type: 'order.status', id: eventId, order: { external_order_id: pm.collectionVariables.get('orderId') || pm.environment.get('orderId'), state: 'accepted' } };
// Serialize once. This exact string is what gets signed AND sent.
// Optional per contract 3.2; must be within the +/-5 minute replay window.
console.log('Deduped: this event id was already processed (contract 6.0).');
console.log('202 means QUEUED, not applied. Effects land shortly after (contract 6.0).');

request.description:
Direction: Reseller -> WeAreDA.

order.status (contract 6.1). ONE event per transition, each with its own event id.

TWO columns. integration_status always moves; orders.status - the customer-facing
one - moves only when the tenant registered orderStatusWrite: true (folder 00).

  state                                    integration_status  orders.status
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  accepted | acknowledged | ack            accepted            confirmed
  shipped | fulfilled                      completed           shipped
  delivered | completed                    completed           delivered
  cancelled | canceled                     cancelled           cancelled
  returned | return | refunded |
    not_delivered | undelivered            returned            refunded
  rejected | failed | error                manual_review       (unchanged)
  anything else                            NOT MAPPED          (unchanged)

shipped and delivered COLLAPSE to completed, so orders.status is derived from the
RAW state, never from integration_status. fulfilled maps to shipped, not delivered:
the cheaper wrong guess, since the ladder discards a lower rung arriving later.

LADDER      draft -> pending -> confirmed -> processing -> shipped -> delivered
            Only ever ADVANCES. A lower rung after a higher one is ignored.
EXCEPTIONS  cancelled, refunded - apply from ANY rung at ANY time.

This event NEVER changes stock - not even shipped or delivered.

item.description: Every failure mode the contract names, so you can see each one once on purpose instead of at 2am.

request.description:
Direction: WeAreDA -> Reseller.

Means WeAreDA's registered credential does not match your RESELLER_API_KEY. Not retried: the integration goes to manual_review.

Direction: WeAreDA -> Reseller.

Run it as many times as you like: the order count never grows. Check GET /debug/orders.

The `customer` object (contract 4.3, added 2026-09) is OPTIONAL and ADDITIVE:
  - the whole key is OMITTED when the order has no contact;
  - customer.tax_id is NULL when the contact has no fiscal identification - the
    key is always present INSIDE customer, so you can branch on it directly;
  - tax_id.type is a FREE SHORT TOKEN, not an enum (CUIT, CUIL, DNI, CPF, CNPJ,
    NIF, NIE, CIF, RFC, EIN, SSN, VAT, TAX_ID, ...). An unknown value is normal:
    accept it verbatim, never normalise it, NEVER reject the order over it;
  - tax_id.country is ISO 3166-1 alpha-2;
  - the values are a SNAPSHOT taken when the order was created (4.3.1). Do not
    expect them to match a later read of the customer, and never 'correct' a
    stored order from one. An order that arrived with no fiscal id may report
    one later - the snapshot freezes a value, not an absence.

If you cannot invoice without a fiscal id, set syncConfig.orders.requiresTaxId:
true (4.3.2, folder 00) - WeAreDA then never delivers such an order, and
delivers it automatically within a minute of the tenant completing the contact.
Rejecting the delivery is the wrong answer: a non-auth 4xx is not retried.

The identifier below is deliberately fake. The sandbox MASKS it in every log
line and in GET /debug/orders (20-******78-9) and keeps the real value only on
the order it invoices against (11.8).
